subject: Targeted mitigation authorization: Finport (model v4.3) p95 divergence action plan
messages:
From: Tom Reynolds <tom.reynolds@finport.com>
To: Irene Choi <irene_choi@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>, Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 25 Jun 2028 08:12:00 -0700
Subject: Realtime alert — model v4.3 p95 divergence observed on /autocomplete (Finport-prod)

Hi team,

Quick note from Finport ops: since ~2028-06-24 22:00 UTC we started seeing an uptick in p95 for the /autocomplete endpoint tied to the model variant tagged v4.3-quant-c. Baseline p95 historically ~240ms; current p95 peaked at 980ms with intermittent timeouts for longer prompts. We've attached a CSV extract of sampled traces and token-level timing (finport_p95_logs_2028-06-24.csv).

Impact: ~3% of sessions see degraded UX (timeouts & slow suggestions) which is affecting conversion on our search form during business hours. We are on a committed usage plan and relying on the p95 SLA.

As a remediation ask: can Redwood provide an authorization path for one of the following so we can get Finport-prod back to baseline quickly?
- Immediate traffic quarantine of v4.3-quant-c and pin traffic to v4.2-stable for Finport-prod (short window)
- Or a targeted rollback of model for Finport-prod for a 30–60 minute window while you investigate

Please advise next steps and who on your side needs to approve a provisional rollback or traffic quarantine.

Thanks,
Tom
Tom Reynolds
Principal SRE, Finport
ops@finport.com

---
Attachments: finport_p95_logs_2028-06-24.csv (text/csv, 120KB)

From: Irene Choi <irene_choi@redwood.com>

Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 25 Jun 2028 08:25:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Realtime alert — model v4.3 p95 divergence observed on /autocomplete (Finport-prod)

Tom — thanks for the signal and the attached traces. I pulled the Finport dashboard (https://monitoring.redwood.com/dashboards/finport/v4.3) and can see the p95 spike aligning with the deploy window you referenced.

We take SLA impacts seriously — I'm authorizing a provisional mitigation path while we complete a lightweight root-cause triage:
1) Quarantine v4.3-quant-c for Finport-prod (no new sessions routed to that variant).
2) Pin Finport-prod traffic to v4.2-stable in us-east1.
3) Allow a 45-minute rollback window (start T+1h from approval) if the quarantine does not stabilize p95 to within 15% of baseline.

Ben — can you confirm with the commercial team that the temporary routing change and short rollback window are acceptable under the committed contract (HB-1234567)? I will need a quick sign-off so we can proceed. Monica/Karthik, please coordinate the runbook and take the lead on the execution.

I will issue the approval once Ben confirms commercial ok.

Irene

From: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>

Subject: Re: Realtime alert — model v4.3 p95 divergence observed on /autocomplete (Finport-prod)

Team — quick technical note from runtime: I'm seeing two correlated signals in the traces Tom attached and our internal logs (variant-profile-v4.3.pdf):
- Token emission time increases after step 256 for longer prompts; this aligns with a degraded attention kernel path on the quantized variant.
- The issue is isolated to the v4.3-quant-c variant (other variants of v4.3 and v4.2-stable are normal).

Short remediation options (ordered by speed):
A) Quarantine v4.3-quant-c for Finport-prod (zero config change on client side; router drops variant from pool).
B) Pin traffic to v4.2-stable in the affected region (us-east1) while we backfill a hotfix/optimize kernels.
C) If quarantine doesn't bring p95 back to baseline within 20 minutes, we should trigger a targeted rollback for Finport-prod to v4.2-stable for a controlled window (45 minutes).

Execution notes: runbook-rollback-window.md contains the exact commands and pre/post checks. Monica — please stage the runbook steps and prep the Canary monitor alarms. I'll be on the incident channel to coordinate.

Karthik Iyer
Principal Engineer, Serving Runtime
karthik_iyer@redwood.com

Attachments: variant-profile-v4.3.pdf (application/pdf, 340KB); runbook-rollback-window.md (text/markdown, 6KB)

From: Irene Choi <irene_choi@redwood.com>

Date: Tue, 25 Jun 2028 09:45:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Targeted mitigation authorization: Finport (model v4.3) p95 divergence action plan

Tom — confirming we will proceed as follows (authorized):
1) At 2028-06-25 10:00 UTC we will quarantine variant v4.3-quant-c for Finport-prod and pin traffic to v4.2-stable in us-east1.
2) We will monitor p95 and short-circuit the quarantine if we see any regression elsewhere. If p95 does not return to within 15% of baseline after 20 minutes, we will initiate a controlled rollback to v4.2-stable for a 45-minute window (start time to be announced on the incident channel).
3) Ben has confirmed commercial is OK; no change to committed billing for this temporary mitigation.

Tom/Finport Ops: please standby on the incident channel for a short validation (we will ask you to validate key flows once the quarantine is active). Monica/Karthik will run the steps (runbook-rollback-window.md attached).

I'll publish a short incident note after the window and circle back with a proposed follow-up (kernel investigation / quantization QA) next week.
